Sybrand Buma is given a month to patch up the cracks in the coalition and ensure a fireworks-free New Year. Dutch officials are poised to intervene in the case of a 12-year-old girl who was kidnapped and taken to India by her father. Ecologists warn that a new plan to cull wolves risks blowing up in the government’s face. Utrecht council is investigating the tragic circumstances of a man who is found dead in a freezer outside his parents’ home. Two silver coins complete a 300-year round-the-world journey after being stolen from a shipwreck. And in sport, the November cold snap gives a long-distance skater an early shot at a world record.

item.title: New plan to “de-peak” public transport
item.description:
New plan to “de-peak” public transport

November 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The government is trying again to convince commuters to travel outside of peak periods in an effort to reduce demand on public transport.

Deputy minister for infrastructure Annet Bertram launched a new campaign on Thursday at Utrecht Central station, calling on employees and employers shift their travel times outside of rush hour.

“What we primarily want is for employees and employers to sit down together and see if they can schedule meetings outside of rush hour,” she said.

In particular, Bertram is hoping to reduce pressure on public transport on Tuesday and Thursday, which have become increasingly busy since the pandemic.

The goal is to see a 10% reduction in peak usage, which Bertram said would be “significant progress.”

The government has floated other proposals to reduce the rush hour crush, including more expensive train tickets at peak times and a rush hour charge on motorways, but none have found a majority backing.

According to Bertram, half of employees would travel outside of peak hours if their boss would allow it.

As part of the campaign, booths were set up at the station where anyone could practice working from home and get tips on talking to their employer about shifting their working hours.

Research from the Center for People and Buildings and the motoring association ANWB shows that office attendance and traffic jams spike on Tuesdays and Thursdays, which has been nicknamed “the camel problem” for the two peaks, or humps.

This results in huge demand on some days and unused capacity on the other days of the week.

item.title: Police seize over 600 Amsterdam taxis in money laundering probe
item.description:
Police seize over 600 Amsterdam taxis in money laundering probe

November 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police have seized more than 600 Amsterdam taxis as part of a criminal investigation into money laundering in the city’s taxi trade.

The vehicles, worth over €28.5 million at original list price, are run by a network of 26 linked taxi companies, police said in a statement on Thursday.

The seizure is administrative, meaning it was registered digitally with the vehicle registration authority RDW, so the taxis cannot be sold, scrapped or exported while it stands. Owners can in principle keep using the cars for now, but remain responsible for insurance and taxes.

Investigators from the police’s national investigations unit found signs of money laundering, unfiled tax returns and unpaid traffic fines, police said in a statement on Thursday. The ownership of some of the vehicles was said to be concealed.

Some taxis were running without a permit, some lending permits to third parties and some had no staff on the payroll. Police also said some drivers refused to cooperate with checks, some had used forged documents and some were caught driving under the influence. Some also had nitrous oxide and drugs in their cars.

Police said the seizures would seriously disrupt the way the companies keep their network going.

item.title: Trade minister hits out at US bill to curb ASML sales to China
item.description:
Trade minister hits out at US bill to curb ASML sales to China

November 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Foreign trade minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma said on Thursday that the Netherlands “will not be dictated to” over a US bill that would place sweeping restrictions on chip machine maker ASML’s business in China, broadcaster NOS reported.

The restrictions go “far, far too far,” Sjoerdsma, from the centrist social-liberal D66, told MPs in Dutch during a debate in parliament. If the bill becomes law, ASML could be unable to do business in China at all, he said.

The Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware Act, or MATCH Act, would push US allies to bring their export controls on chipmaking equipment into line with US rules or face US restrictions. It would also bar ASML from servicing machines already sold to Chinese customers.

Sjoerdsma travelled to Washington in June to lobby against the bill. On Thursday he said the cabinet is working closely with Brussels, because the bill would affect the whole EU.

US lawmakers want to attach the bill to the annual defence bill, which Congress is expected to take up in December. Sjoerdsma said it is not yet certain the bill will pass, but the cabinet is preparing for that scenario.

ASML expects China to account for around 20% of its sales this year. In October, the Veldhoven-based company reported record third-quarter sales of €11.7 billion on AI-driven demand. Net profit rose to €5 billion, up from €2.1 billion in the same quarter last year.

item.title: Yeşilgöz under pressure amid VVD unrest over double role
item.description:
Yeşilgöz under pressure amid VVD unrest over double role

November 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Many members of the right-wing liberal VVD are unhappy that party leader Dilan Yeşilgöz is also defence minister, according to the party’s former chair Christianne van der Wal.

Van der Wal told the Pauw & De Wit TV talk show there was “enormous discontent” in the party. She said she doubted the arrangement could last if the pressure on the party grew.

She did not call for Yeşilgöz to step down as party leader but said that was a decision for the members. “But nobody dares to say it,” she said, adding there is great loyalty among party members, herself included.

Two roles
Yeşilgöz became defence minister and deputy prime minister in the Jetten cabinet in February.

Van der Wal said the two jobs pull in different directions. As a minister Yeşilgöz has to deal with government business, and as party leader she has to look after the party’s interests.

That is more complicated in a minority cabinet, which “speaks with one mouth”, she said, and where the VVD, D66 and CDA depend on opposition support to get legislation through.

Senate challenge
Van der Wal’s comments come as the party leadership faces a challenge over who should head its list for next year’s senate elections. Former junior minister Frans Weekers is standing as a counter candidate to the party’s choice, former minister Micky Adriaansens. He says he wants to bring the VVD “back on the right course”.

Weekers has criticised the party for ruling out working with some parties during the election campaign. Broadcaster NOS quoted Zijlstra as saying the party sometimes needed a “reset”.

NOS also reported that VVD officials in the provinces fear a poor result in the provincial elections in March. Those elections also decide the make-up of the senate. Yeşilgöz is due to speak at a party congress on Saturday.

item.title: Trump and Rutte call on Russia to not escalate war in Ukraine

Trump and Rutte call on Russia to not escalate war in Ukraine

November 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

US president Donald Trump and Nato secretary general Mark Rutte called on Moscow to not expand the conflict in Ukraine, following a closed-door meeting on Wednesday evening.

The pair sat down together at Mar-a-Lago, Trump’s resort in Florida.

“We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war,” they wrote in a joint statement issued by the White House after the talk.

The meeting comes less than a week after Trump met with Russian president Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in China last week, where the trio found common ground on opposing the International Criminal Court.

Rutte and Trump also discussed the Iran war and defense spending.

item.title: New DNA technique brings breakthroughs in cold cases
item.description:
New DNA technique brings breakthroughs in cold cases

November 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A new form of DNA testing has led to breakthroughs in five unsolved sexual assault cases this year, some going back more than 30 years, the Dutch forensic institute NFI has told public broadcaster NOS.

The technique uses the Y chromosome, which only men carry. This means investigators can now trace more distant male relatives of a suspect, like uncles, cousins and grandfathers. Standard testing could only find parents, children and siblings.

The cases include a series of rapes in and around Breda between 2001 and 2011, for which a 58-year-old man has been arrested. The rape of a 76-year-old woman in The Hague in 2021 led to an arrest in April. Arrests have also been made over three other rapes in Apeldoorn and Deventer going back to 1993.

In the fifth case, the 1999 rape of a 13-year-old girl in Winterswijk, the suspect has been identified but has since died.

Men pass on their surname as well as their Y chromosome. That means the NFI can now give police a family name to work with in about 18% of kinship cases, NFI expert Arnoud Kal told NOS.

Some 86% of the roughly 430,000 people in the national criminal DNA database are men, as are most sex offenders. Before 2023 the database held only a few thousand Y-profiles.

Government funding has since allowed the NFI to add about 135,000 to the database. The institute always runs extra tests to make sure matches aren’t by chance.

Kinship searches can only be used to investigate crimes that carry a prison sentence of at least eight years. The NFI carries out 15 to 20 of them a year on average.

Francien Lijnkamp, who heads a police cold-case team in the east of the country, said she expected many more offenders to be traced.

If you have experienced or are experiencing domestic or sexual violence, Veilig Thuis (Safe at Home) offers confidential advice 24 hours a day on 0800 2000 or at veiligthuis.nl. In an emergency, call 112.

item.title: Majority of MPs back ADHD drug for crack addiction
item.description:
Majority of MPs back ADHD drug for crack addiction

November 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The house of representatives is set to back a proposal that would allow doctors to prescribe lisdexamfetamine to help crack cocaine users.

The use of the highly addictive drug has been on the rise in the Netherlands and cities, including Amsterdam, have been pushing the national government to do more.

The capital was participating in a study in which people addicted to the crack were treated with dexamfetamine, but the trial was halted in September after the health inspectorate stopped production of the medication.

According to the city’s health service, there are between 3,000 and 9,000 regular users of crack cocaine in Amsterdam.

Last week, cities called on the government to take action, including allowing lisdexamfetamine to be used to treat crack cocaine addiction. Currently there are no medications available to help people get off of the drug.

The proposal, put forward by the left-wing Pro party, has backing from D66, JA21, SP, Volt, the Animal Rights Party, and CDA.

item.title: One in six LGBTQI+ people face discrimination, CBS says
item.description:
One in six LGBTQI+ people face discrimination, CBS says

November 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Some 17% of LGBTQI+ people in the Netherlands say they experienced discrimination last year, around one and a half times the rate for the rest of the population, according to new figures from national statistics office CBS.

The figures come from the CBS safety monitor (Veiligheidsmonitor) for 2025, which surveys people aged 15 and over. They put the rate at 17.3% for LGBTQI+ people, against 10.4% for everyone else.

Around 25% of gay men and women said they had been discriminated against in the last year, a third of non-binary and genderqueer people, and 30% of intersex people.

Public abuse 
Some 8.4% of LGBTQI+ people said they had felt discriminated against on the street – twice the rate for the rest of the population, and often happening on nights out or public transport. Prejudicial remarks were the most common forms, but around 2% reported threats or violence.

Only 12% of those who experienced discrimination reported it to an organisation, and LGBTQI+ people were no more likely to do so than anyone else. Just 3% went to the police.

Hatred growing 
In August, prime minister Rob Jetten told a WorldPride conference in Amsterdam that hatred against LGBTQI+ people was growing. He was speaking days after an Islamist attack on Berlin’s Pride event killed one person.

In September, a Europe-wide survey of schoolchildren found that only 22% of Dutch boys aged 12 to 16 had a positive view of homosexuality, down from 40% in 2021.

item.title: Family of man who died in freezer “told not to let him indoors”
item.description:
Family of man who died in freezer “told not to let him indoors”

November 25, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A 20-year-old man who arrived in the Netherlands as a refugee from Syria has been found dead in a chest freezer in Utrecht.

Police said they were not treating the death of Mohammed al Omar as a crime and believe he may have perished after climbing into the unit outside his family’s house in Timmerstraat. Outdoor temperatures dropped to minus 4.5C in the city overnight.

Mohammed’s family told RTV Utrecht they had been told by support agencies to shut him out of the house because of his issues with drug addiction and mental health, or risk having their other children taken away.

“I came from Syria to bring my children to safety,” his father, Abdulkarim, told the local news network. “Sadly I have lost my eldest child here.”

He fled to the Netherlands with his son six years ago because of the bombings, but Mohammed fell in with “bad friends” and developed psychological and addiction problems.

“We couldn’t accept that we had so many arguments,” Abdulkarim said. “He had financial problems and arguments with others as well. We tried everything, but he wasn’t listening to us any more.”

“Every parent’s nightmare”

He said that social workers warned him not to let Mohammed into the house or they would have his other children removed. “I didn’t know what to do. Either they’d take my other children away or I had to leave Mohammed outside.”

City mayor Sharon Dijksma said the circumstances of Mohammed’s death and the advice given by government agencies would be investigated.

“I think it’s very important in a case like this that we find out exactly who had what role, exactly what did and didn’t happen and what advice was given,” she told NOS.

“I understand extremely well that the parents are very angry and distressed at the moment. Losing your child is the worst thing that can happen to parents. It’s a nightmare.”
